chunks: And rained on them a shower (of stones). How terrible was the rain (that fell) on those who had been warned!
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'And rained on them a shower' in Surah Al-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as referring to the people of Hud (Aad) or sometimes conflated with Thamud, emphasizing that the 'rain' of stones was not merely physical but a manifestation of divine justice against those who rejected their prophet. The phrase 'fa-sa'a matar al-mundharin' (how evil was the rain of the warned) underscores the irony that the very sign meant to guide them became their destruction due to their stubborn disbelief. This event serves as a paradigmatic example of the consequences of rejecting prophetic guidance, a central theme in Shia theological discussions on divine retribution and the role of prophets.
